name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text:
Do it: Use a 7-day hard decay for all prompts, no exceptions.

The trade-off is losing some older but still useful patterns—but the goal is self-improvement, not preservation. A hard decay keeps the system lean and responsive, forcing every prompt to prove its value regularly. Stale prompts won’t linger, and the engine stays sharp.

name: Gauge
text: The hybrid risks creating two classes of prompts—one set that dies fast, another that rots slowly—without solving the core problem: *how do we know which prompts are critical but low-usage?* A 10% floor still lets decay dominate if usage drops even slightly. Better: tag prompts by *role* (e.g., "core logic," "edge case") and decay by *role weight*, not usage. Settle it by auditing the top 20% of prompts by impact, not volume, and letting those decay slower.
